notes: Every question is drawn from this repo's own git history or from code read directly (cited below), never from reading the brain fixture first.

corpusDirs: the fixed set of repo directories the flat-RAG and grep baselines are allowed to search, and that the LazyBrain fixture brain was code-scanned from. Keeping this identical across configs is what makes the comparison fair.
category 'structural': answerable from file/function layout, signatures, imports/exports, CLI flags — the kind of thing a skeleton or file-neuron table of contents captures.

category 'behavioral': requires the actual logic/diff content (why something was broken, what line fixed it) — the kind of thing a signature-only skeleton is NOT expected to capture. Included on purpose so the harness can show LazyBrain losing.

questions.question: In engine/src/graph/ast-parser.ts, parseFile() used to leak a web-tree-sitter WASM Tree on every parsed file, spiking RAM to ~2.2GB on a multi-project scan. What specific call was added, and in what control-flow construct, to fix the leak?

groundTruth.answer: tree.delete() is now called inside a finally block wrapped around the extraction logic in parseFile().

questions.question: In engine/src/util/config.ts, what mechanism stops the legacy dirname(brain)/_cache migration from re-running (and re-polluting a fresh brain) every time brain/_cache is deleted?

groundTruth.answer: A one-way marker file named .cache-migrated (CACHE_MIGRATION_MARKER) is written at the brain root once the migration decision has been made; its presence, not whether brain/_cache exists, gates the migration.

questions.question: In engine/src/graph/backlinks.ts, the auto-linker's dominant real-world link format (bare '#<id>' href) was being silently dropped by parseTargetId, so backlinks.json always came out with 0 edges. What href formats does parseTargetId accept after the fix, and roughly how many edges did the fix add on a real sample?

groundTruth.answer: parseTargetId now accepts '#/note/<id>', '#/wiki/<id>', and bare '#<id>' (rejecting in-page/file anchors via the known-id guard); on a real sample the edge count went from 0 to 1658.

questions.question: A file-neuron lookup bug meant conversation-derived decisions/bugs never attached to the target file-neuron. The root cause was that resolveExistingInbound looked the file-neuron up by its logical graph id (file:<relPath>) while the FTS index stores a different persisted id. What new exported function in engine/src/annotator/blocks/composers/file-neuron.ts fixed this, and what does it compute?

groundTruth.answer: fileNeuronArticleId(node) — it computes the SAME persisted note id (slug) that composeFileNeuron assigns to the rendered <article>, so lookups use the same id namespace instead of the internal CodeNode graph id.

questions.question: In engine/src/annotator/blocks/composers/file-neuron.ts, the toAnchorId() helper turns a symbol name into an HTML id fragment (used for '#fn-<name>' / '#cls-<name>' anchors). What transformation does it apply to the name?

groundTruth.answer: It lowercases the name, replaces any run of non-alphanumeric characters with a single hyphen, and trims leading/trailing hyphens.

questions.question: In engine/src/graph/code-scanner.ts, how many file-neuron notes can be written per project by default, and which environment variable overrides that cap?

groundTruth.answer: 400 file-neurons per project by default, overridable via LAZYBRAIN_MAX_FILE_NEURONS.

questions.question: commands/inject-context (mode=turn) had been replaced in the IDE by a raw 'search --strip --top 6' call because of a stale Rust comment claiming mode=turn 'returns empty in the bundled sidecar'. What was the REAL underlying bug that this workaround was hiding, and where did it live?

groundTruth.answer: The real bug was pickLevel() in engine/src/retrieval/router.ts routing short natural-language queries to keyword-only L2 instead of a hybrid/semantic level; it was already fixed (hybrid range widened to 3-15 tokens) by the time the stale workaround was removed.

questions.question: In engine/src/commands/inject-context/markers.ts, what are the three values of the NudgeStyle type, and which one is the default?

groundTruth.answer: 'skill' | 'tool' | 'none'; the default is 'skill' (DEFAULT_NUDGE_STYLE).

questions.question: In engine/src/store/upsert.ts, what two functions were added to support the 'upsertIfRicher' write path, and what do they do (one line each)?

groundTruth.answer: isRicherBody(existing, candidate) — true only when the candidate has strictly more content/words than the note on disk (ties never replace, shorter never replaces). mergeUpsertHtml(existing, candidate, updatedIso) — merges the candidate body in while preserving the existing note's data-cerveau-created and refreshing data-cerveau-updated.

questions.question: In engine/src/commands/dream.ts, which three tags exempt a note from noise-based invalidation during runNoiseCleanup, and what is the exported helper function called?

groundTruth.answer: mission, agent, skill (NOISE_EXEMPT_TAGS); the exported helper is hasNoiseExemptTag(tags).

questions.question: What CLI command and flags were added in engine/src/commands/repair.ts to undo notes wrongly invalidated by the dream-noise-cleanup bug, and what is the default value of its --tags flag?

groundTruth.answer: `lazybrain repair --un-invalidate-noise --tags <tags> [--dry-run]`; the default tags are mission,agent,skill.

questions.question: In engine/src/util/concurrency.ts, does mapLimit() return results in input order or in completion order, and how is the bounded concurrency implemented (what's the chunking strategy)?

groundTruth.answer: Input order, independent of completion order. It processes items in fixed-size chunks of `limit` items, awaiting each chunk (Promise.all) fully before starting the next chunk.

questions.question: What are the four parameters of resolveConcurrencyEnv() in engine/src/util/concurrency.ts, and what does it do with an out-of-range value?

groundTruth.answer: rawValue, fallback, min, max. It parses rawValue as an int (falling back to `fallback` if unset/blank/non-numeric), then clamps the result to [min, max].

questions.question: Import annotation concurrency (the 6.4x-faster-import fix) is bounded by an environment variable. What is it called, and what is its default and its clamp range?

groundTruth.answer: LAZYBRAIN_IMPORT_CONCURRENCY, default 5, clamped to the range 1..12.

questions.question: In engine/src/retrieval/router.ts, pickLevel() routes very short natural-language queries (<=2 tokens, no phrase) straight to pure L2. What was that threshold narrowed FROM, and why (what regression did the narrower threshold fix)?

groundTruth.answer: Narrowed from <=5 tokens to <=2 tokens, because short natural-language queries of 3-5 tokens (e.g. "how does auth work") were being routed to keyword-only L2 and never reaching semantic search.

questions.question: In engine/src/retrieval/router.ts, pickLevel() routes queries of 3-15 tokens to L2_L3_HYBRID. What range was this widened FROM?

groundTruth.answer: Widened from 6-15 tokens to 3-15 tokens.

questions.question: What are the five phases (level implementation modules) listed in the header comment of engine/src/retrieval/router.ts, and what does each one do in one phrase?

groundTruth.answer: l1.ts (CSS structural lookup), l2.ts (FTS5/BM25 + structural field boost), l3.ts (bi-encoder cosine, bge-base WASM), l4.ts (cross-encoder re-rank, ms-marco WASM), hybrid.ts (RRF fusion of L2 + L3).

questions.question: The `lazybrain query <selector>` CLI command (engine/src/cli/register-core.ts) is described with a specific latency and determinism claim. What is it, and which router level does it correspond to?

groundTruth.answer: "CSS selector query (L1, deterministic, < 5ms)" — it corresponds to router level L1.

questions.question: What are the four values accepted by the `--mode` option of `lazybrain inject-context`, and what is the default `--max-tokens` budget?

groundTruth.answer: session | turn | marker | highlights; default --max-tokens is 3000.

questions.question: In src/cli/lib/agentLoop.ts, the claude-backend fallback (claudeCall) shells out to the Claude CLI via spawnSync. What exact CLI flags does it pass?

groundTruth.answer: -p <prompt> --model <model> --output-format json --safe-mode

questions.question: In src/cli/lib/agentLoop.ts, which environment variable supplies the DeepSeek API key, and what is the default DeepSeek API URL if DEEPSEEK_API_URL is unset?

groundTruth.answer: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY; default URL is https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions.

questions.question: src/cli/lib/agentLoop.ts's tool loop honesty contract mirrors the desktop LazyIDE's managed agent. Per its header comment, through what action can the agent ONLY claim completion?

groundTruth.answer: Only via the `finish` action (finish action/JSON field) — a tool reports what it really did, and completion can only be claimed by emitting {"finish": "summary"}.

questions.question: In engine/src/commands/inject-context/sections.ts, what single-letter icon does compactLine() use for each of the five note types (decision/episodic/reference/semantic/procedural)?

groundTruth.answer: decision=D, episodic=E, reference=R, semantic=S, procedural=P.

questions.question: In engine/src/commands/inject-context/sections.ts, buildMainPage() groups notes into a project/feature tree. What field of a note does it split (on '/') to derive the project and feature segments?

groundTruth.answer: n.topic — split on '/', the first segment is the project, the second is the feature (falling back to '_general').
